scope: Read-only diagnosis; no product or test changes, no new baseline full-suite run, no test suppression.

baseline_verification.meaning: 402 tracked source/test/build files match the saved pre-CU index exactly; this includes the original staged work. No native extension was rebuilt or substituted during this audit.

third_full_run.outcome: Terminated after persistent native Qt mutex wait; not counted as a completed full regression.
third_full_run.boundary: Sampling confirms the blocked location, not the mutex owner or root cause. The baseline was not shown to reproduce this wait; do not label it a verified baseline deadlock.

fourth_full_run.theme_diagnostic: The 60-second faulthandler dump occurred during test_system_theme_uses_stable_controls_and_tracks_appearance (theme.apply_application_theme -> QApplication.setStyleSheet -> MainWindow.eventFilter). That test later PASSED and the full suite finished. faulthandler_timeout emits a stack dump; it does not abort a test. This run was slow theme processing, not a demonstrated deadlock.

baseline_failure_evidence.description: Previously completed pre-change UI comparison reproduced these same five failures.

unchanged_trigger_path.interpretation: The observed theme/icon callback chain predates CU changes; that alone does not prove the rare mutex wait is a baseline failure.

recommendation: Retain the completed fourth full-run result as coverage. If the native wait recurs, collect its lock owner and per-file surviving QWidget/MainWindow counts, then compare the verified pre-change tree. Large surviving widget/theme callback accumulation is a hypothesis, not a measured cause. Per-file process isolation may be used for additional coverage without altering or skipping tests; it was not required after the fourth run completed.
